title: Air Starter Motor Heat Shield — Removal
abstract: Removal of the air starter motor heat shield, including the duct standoff release, the fretting record at the shield edge and the harness handling that protects the starter feeder.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to remove the air starter motor heat shield for access to the starter motor, for shield replacement or to record the fretting condition at the standoff positions.
sections.job_setup_note: The shield is thin and its edges are sharp; wear cut resistant gloves. Let the engine cool before entry into the lower fan cowl area. Record the fretting condition at the two standoff positions before anything is disturbed, because that record is the only evidence of the rate at which the condition develops and it is asked for at every engine change.
sections.procedure: 1. Let the engine cool and open the fan cowl, supporting it on the stay. 2. WARNING: THE SHIELD EDGES ARE SHARP. WEAR CUT RESISTANT GLOVES. 3. Photograph and record the fretting condition at the two duct standoff positions against the scale card. 4. Release the cable ties retaining the starter harness where it crosses the shield. 5. CAUTION: DO NOT PULL THE STARTER HARNESS CLEAR BY HAND. THE FEEDER IS STIFF AND WILL TAKE A SET THAT LOADS THE CONNECTOR. 6. Loosen the two duct standoffs at the shield edge. 7. Remove the shield fasteners, working from the aft edge forward, and keep them in the parts tray. 8. Lower the shield clear of the duct and remove it from the cowl area. 9. Examine the shield for cracking at the fastener holes and at the standoff seats and record what you find. 10. Cover the exposed starter motor drive if the cowl will be left open.
sections.close_out: Leave the harness supported and the cowl on its stay if the installation does not follow immediately. Record the removal, the shield part number, the fretting condition and any cracking in the aircraft technical log, and attach the photographs.

safety_precautions: The shield edges are sharp; wear cut resistant gloves.
Let the engine cool before entry into the lower cowl area.

title: Air Starter Motor Heat Shield — Removal

issue.reason: Recording of the standoff fretting condition retained and a disposition statement added so that a finding inside the recorded band no longer reads as an open defect.

sections.close_out: Leave the harness supported and the cowl on its stay if the installation does not follow immediately. Record the removal, the shield part number, the fretting condition and any cracking in the aircraft technical log, and attach the photographs. Disposition: fretting at the two duct standoff positions within the bands on the scale card requires no action on the delivered shield and standoff arrangement. It is the known behaviour of that arrangement, the shield remains serviceable for life with it, and the heat shield change of MOD-168252 is a production change that is not offered as a retrofit, so no in-service embodiment answers it today. A separate proposal, MOD-169548, is open to apply the standoff move to the delivered shield; until it is decided, record the condition, attach the photographs and close the entry. Cracking at a fastener hole or at a standoff seat is a different matter and must be reported.
